key_highlights: ASX treads water amid persistent interest rate fears; RBA Governor Bullock's hawkish stance signals higher-for-longer policy
Iron ore downside persists, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX valuations
Sydney housing market in 'bloodbath' with auction reality check; mortgage rates easing slightly but CD rates at 4.40% APY
Super contributions surge >33% post-budget tax changes; government-backed digital pension scheme proposed as parallel to compulsory super
Gold exploration active: Platina, Broken Hill, Forrestania, Great Southern, Larvotto all advancing WA/SA/NSW projects
Consumer stress: Dollar General CEO flags red flags, Christmas retailer files Chapter 11, discount fashion chain closes 120 stores
Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire chairman at 96; global 'four horsemen' risk narrative intensifies
Diesel/petrol price shock rising, compounding cost-of-living pressure on households

sectors.trend: Iron ore weakness continues to weigh on major miners; however, gold and critical minerals exploration is robust with multiple WA/SA/NSW discoveries (10.72g/t Great Southern, Broken Hill sulphide upgrade, Dalaroo rare earths, Larvotto antimony-gold first concentrate)
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from iron ore downside; gold juniors (PLA.AX, BHP-related, FRT.AX, LRV.AX, DAR.AX) attract speculative flows; rare earths (DAR.AX) offer strategic diversification

sectors.trend: Higher-for-longer rates support NIM but housing 'bloodbath' in Sydney and auction softening raise credit-risk concerns; super contribution surge benefits fund managers; digital pension scheme could disrupt super industry
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from rate environment but face housing-linked credit risk; super fund managers (HUB.AX, PPT.AX) gain from contribution surge; digital pension proposal (headline 66) is a structural threat to compulsory super model

sectors.trend: Diesel/petrol shock rising; energy giants betting billions on longer oil routes; EV adoption accelerating in Australia as consumers flee bowser; EV profitability remains strained globally
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, SXG.AX face fuel demand transition risk; upstream oil (WDS.AX) benefits from route diversification; EV supply chain names face margin compression

sectors.trend: Consumer confidence deteriorating: Dollar General CEO flags red flags, Christmas retailer Chapter 11, 80-year discount chain closing 120 stores; airfares soaring ahead of grand final; cost-of-living pressure from fuel
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX, IAG.AX face demand softness; discount retailers under pressure; travel names (QAN.AX, QLT.AX) see seasonal volume but margin squeeze

sectors.trend: Migraine prevalence doubles (undercounting corrected); Oracle cloud revenue +121% with $664B backlog; AI adoption accelerating across services (ServiceTitan, IDEXX); Interactive Brokers 77% pretax margin
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, WES.AX (pharma) benefit from chronic disease trends; tech exposure via Oracle (ORCL), IBKR, TTAN positive but US-centric; limited direct ASX tech play

sectors.trend: Sydney housing 'bloodbath' and auction reality check signal residential correction; rental market disruption proposed (cutting out agents); housing policy under political pressure
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, DGL.AX) face occupancy and yield pressure; residential developers (DHG.AX, LVH.AX) at risk; rental reform could reshape property services

key_themes: RBA hawkish pivot: Bullock signals higher rates as new normal, pressuring rate-sensitive sectors
Iron ore structural downside: China demand concerns persist, capping materials sector upside
Housing correction: Sydney auction market reality check, rising fuel costs, credit tightening
Superannuation reform wave: 33% contribution surge, digital pension proposal, system fitness debate
Gold & critical minerals exploration boom: WA/SA/NSW pipeline active, strategic government interest
Consumer stress: retail bankruptcies, fuel shock, cost-of-living squeeze
Global macro risk: Trump trade war, 'four horsemen' narrative, Buffett succession uncertainty
Demographic shift: deaths outpacing births, ageing population, baby bonus debate

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds, reduce leverage, favour rate-insensitive sectors (healthcare, consumer staples)
Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX exposure; rotate into gold and critical minerals names
Underweight residential REITs and developers; monitor NAB.AX/CBA.AX credit provisions
Favour discount/essential retail (WES.AX, IAG.AX) over discretionary; monitor retail sales data
Diversify away from China-exposed miners; hold AUD-hedged positions; maintain cash buffer
Monitor digital pension scheme legislation; assess impact on HUB.AX, PPT.AX, QAN.AX fund flows

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and critical minerals exploration names
opportunities.rationale: Active WA/SA/NSW pipeline with multiple high-grade discoveries; strategic government interest in rare earths and antimony; hedge against geopolitical risk

opportunities.recommendation: Add defensive healthcare and consumer staples exposure
opportunities.rationale: Migraine prevalence doubling signals chronic disease growth; staples resilient in consumer stress environment; rate-insensitive

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical long on super fund managers
opportunities.rationale: 33% contribution surge post-budget provides near-term revenue tailwind; digital pension scheme is early-stage and unlikely to disrupt within 12 months

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore major exposure; trim BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX
defensive_moves.rationale: Persistent iron ore downside, China demand uncertainty, and Trump trade war risk cap upside; rotate into gold/critical minerals

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight residential REITs and property developers
defensive_moves.rationale: Sydney housing 'bloodbath', auction softening, and rising rates pressure occupancy and valuations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain 10-15% cash allocation; lock in 4.40% APY CDs
defensive_moves.rationale: Higher-for-longer rate environment rewards cash; CD yields at 4.40% offer risk-free return amid market uncertainty

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely range-bound to modestly lower over 1-3 months. RBA hawkish bias, iron ore weakness, and Sydney housing stress cap upside. Gold miners and super managers provide selective pockets of strength. Consumer stress and fuel shock add downside risk. Expect volatility around RBA communications.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautious. Structural iron ore decline, demographic headwinds (deaths outpacing births), and super system reform create uncertainty. Gold/critical minerals and healthcare offer structural growth. Housing correction may stabilise by H2 2027. Global trade war risk remains the key wildcard.
